subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the minor and the cofactor of the element 5 in the matrix with rows (1, 0, −2), (3, −1, 2) and (4, 5, 6).

mark_split.label: Apply the sign to get the cofactor

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 27, book p.36. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives one mark to the minor and one to the sign, because the question names two different quantities and the sign is the part students lose. POSITION: 5 is the entry in row 3, column 2, so it is a₃₂; deleting that row and that column leaves the 2×2 determinant with rows (1, −2) and (3, 2). CHECKED: the minor was evaluated twice, as (1)(2) − (−2)(3) = 2 + 6 = 8 and again as the determinant of the remaining block read down its columns, both giving 8; the cofactor is (−1)³⁺² × 8 = −8. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the minor and the cofactor of the element 5.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the minor of 5
steps.margin_note: First mark. Locate 5 first: it is in row 3, column 2, so it is a₃₂. Delete that row and that column and take the determinant of what is left. The minor carries no sign.
steps.memory_tip: Cover the row and the column that the element sits in. What is left is the minor.
lines: The element 5 is in row 3, column 2,
so it is a₃₂. Delete row 3 and column 2.

recall.must_convey: That 5 sits at row 3 column 2, and deleting that row and column leaves a 2×2 determinant whose value 8 is the minor.
accept: five is in row three column two so delete that row and that column
the minor is the two by two determinant left behind, which is eight
cover the third row and second column and evaluate what remains
row three column two delete cheste migilina determinant eight
minor M three two equals one times two minus minus two times three
reject: delete a row and a column

steps.why: The minor of an element is the determinant of the block that survives when its own row and column are removed. It is a plain value with no sign attached.
common_mistakes: Reading 5 as a₂₃ instead of a₃₂ and deleting the wrong row and column.
Putting the sign (−1)³⁺² on the minor, where it does not belong.

steps.label: Apply the sign to get the cofactor
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The cofactor is the minor times (−1) raised to the power (row + column). Here 3 + 2 = 5, which is odd, so the sign is minus and the cofactor is −8.
steps.memory_tip: Row plus column even, keep the sign; odd, change it. Here 3 + 2 = 5 is odd, so the cofactor is −8.
lines: The minor carries no sign. The cofactor
is the minor times (−1) to the power i + j.

recall.must_convey: That the cofactor is (−1) to the power (3 + 2) times the minor, so it equals −8 while the minor stays 8.
accept: the cofactor is minus one to the power three plus two times eight, which is minus eight
three plus two is five which is odd so the sign is negative
minor is eight and cofactor is minus eight
three plus two odd kabatti sign minus, so cofactor minus eight
multiply the minor by the sign from the position

steps.why: The cofactor is the minor with the sign of the position attached, and that sign is what makes the expansion of a determinant work. Minor and cofactor differ only by that sign.
common_mistakes: Giving the same value for both, usually 8 and 8.
Using (−1)²⁺³ from the wrong position, which happens to give the same sign here but is the wrong reason.
